q: עם ההזדקנות מתרחשים שינויים רבים בפרמקוקניטיקה ופרמקודינמיקה של תרופות. מה מבין הבאים נשמר כמעט ללא שינוי?
o: נפח פיזור התרופה בגוף
מטבוליזם כבדי
הספיגה של התרופה
ההפרשה דרך הכליות
explanation:
**Drug absorption** remains largely unchanged with age, whereas distribution, metabolism, and excretion change (pp. 302–303).

**A. Volume of distribution.** Wrong, changing body composition alters distribution: a relative increase in fat increases the volume of distribution of lipid-soluble drugs (p. 302).
**B. Hepatic metabolism.** Wrong, hepatic oxidative metabolism decreases with age and can alter drug clearance (p. 302).
**C. Drug absorption.** Correct, the book explicitly states that drug absorption remains largely unchanged with aging (p. 302).
**D. Renal excretion.** Wrong, renal clearance tends to decline, although individuals differ; it is therefore not the best-preserved process (pp. 303, 1268).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 302–303, 1268.

q: בן 79 מגיע להערכה במרפאה בלווי ביתו, שמספרת על בלבול ומצב רוח ירוד שהופיעו בהדרגה בשנה האחרונה. בשיחה בולטים אפקט דיכאוני וליקוי בקשב. במבחן MMSE השיג תוצאה של 24/30 עם ירידה בזיכרון לטווח קצר והפרעה בחיסור 7 מ- 100. ב- CT מוח נמצאה אטרופיה מוחית. מה מהנתונים תורם לאבחנה של PROBABLE DEMENTIA DUE TO ALZHEIMER DISEASE ?
o: אטרופיה מוחית שנמצאה ב- CT
אפקט דיכאוני
הפרעה בקשב
החמרה הדרגתית במצב הקוגניטיבי
explanation:
**Gradual cognitive worsening** supports probable dementia due to Alzheimer disease. The NIA-AA clinical criteria require insidious onset and documented worsening, while excluding delirium or a major psychiatric explanation for the deficits. The course over the preceding year supports this component of the diagnosis (p. 895, Table 59-1).

**A. Cerebral atrophy on CT.** Wrong, this finding alone does not meet the requirements for insidious onset and worsening cognition; it is not one of the decisive clinical features in Table 59-1 (p. 895).
**B. Depressive affect.** Wrong, depression prompts assessment of whether a psychiatric disorder explains the cognitive impairment; its presence does not specifically support AD (p. 895).
**C. Impaired attention.** Wrong, attention impairment alone does not establish the required course or remove the need to exclude delirium or another cause (p. 895).
**D. Gradual cognitive worsening.** Correct, this is the officially accepted option and matches onset over months to years and a clear history of worsening cognition (p. 895).

A gradual course is a cornerstone of the clinical diagnosis of probable Alzheimer disease in Hazzard (p. 895).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 895.

q: בת 87 מתלוננת שסובלת בשנה האחרונה מחולשה ותשישות כללית. היא ירדה במשקל מירידה במשקל (מ-65 ק"ג ל- 59 ק"ג). מדווחת שירדה בפעילות (מסתגרת בבית, הפסיקה לצאת לקניות, הפסיקה לנהוג ברכב). היא החלה ללכת עם מקל משום שהליכתה לא יציבה, ואף מעדה ונפלה פעם אחת ברחוב ומאז חוששת לצאת מהבית. מדווחת גם על ירידה בזיכרון לטווח הקצר בחודשים האחרונים. מה מהממצאים של החולה מתאימים למאפיינים של FRAILTY לפי FRIED?
o: ירידה במשקל
ירידה בזיכרון לטווח קצר
פחד מנפילות
הליכה לא יציבה
explanation:
The **Fried frailty phenotype** comprises five specific features: unintentional weight loss of more than ten pounds in the prior year, self-reported exhaustion, weakness assessed by grip strength, slow walking speed, and low physical activity (pp. 619-620, Table 42-2).

**A. Weight loss.** Correct, the reported loss exceeds the annual unintentional-weight-loss threshold in the table and corresponds to an explicit phenotype feature (p. 620; comparison with the stem).
**B. Short-term memory decline.** Wrong, it is not one of the five criteria. This does not deny an association between cognition and frailty, which the text explicitly acknowledges (p. 620).
**C. Fear of falling.** Wrong, fear is not one of the defined criteria, even when it reduces activity (pp. 619-620).
**D. Unsteady gait.** Wrong, the criterion is slow gait measured by walking time; unsteadiness alone is not the defined measurement (p. 620).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 619-620.

q: Why do oral NSAIDs require particular caution in older adults with osteoarthritis?
o: They increase gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular risks
They increase gastrointestinal risk while improving renal function
They increase renal risk while improving heart-failure congestion
They increase gastrointestinal risk while improving hypertension
explanation:
**Oral NSAID toxicity** involves more than gastrointestinal bleeding: Hazzard also describes nephrotoxicity and cardiovascular adverse effects (pp. 787–788). NSAIDs can worsen heart failure "by impairing renal sodium and water excretion and contributing to intravascular volume overload" (p. 1173). They can also exacerbate hypertension rather than treating it (p. 1074).

**A. They increase gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular risks.** Correct, bleeding, nephrotoxicity, and cardiovascular complications are all source-described concerns in older patients with OA and comorbidities (pp. 787–788, 1173).
**B. They increase gastrointestinal risk while improving renal function.** Wrong, nephrotoxicity is a stated adverse effect; improved renal function is not the renal effect described here (p. 788).
**C. They increase renal risk while improving heart-failure congestion.** Wrong, impaired sodium and water excretion can worsen congestion and heart failure, rather than improve it (p. 1173).
**D. They increase gastrointestinal risk while improving hypertension.** Wrong, NSAIDs can exacerbate hypertension; the proposed blood-pressure benefit conflicts with the source (p. 1074).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 787, 788, 1173, 1074.
ref: AGS Beers Criteria 2023 — Tables 2–3, pp 2062–2063, 2065 (IMA P005 required article 1)

q: After accounting for study bias, how does Hazzard summarize evidence for intra-articular hyaluronic acid injections in osteoarthritis?
o: Meta-analyses found no clear benefit for osteoarthritis symptoms
Meta-analyses found a clearer benefit for hip osteoarthritis
Meta-analyses found consistent benefit after correction for study bias
Meta-analyses found superiority supporting use as first-line treatment
explanation:
**Viscosupplementation** has a biological rationale because hyaluronic acid is a constituent of synovial fluid, but that does not establish clinical benefit. Meta-analyses found "no clear benefit of intra-articular hyaluronic acid injection for the treatment of OA symptoms" after addressing bias, especially in hip osteoarthritis (p. 789). The source still allows that selected patients may benefit from a trial after other options fail.

**A. Meta-analyses found no clear benefit for osteoarthritis symptoms.** Correct, This reflects the bias-adjusted evidence summary, without asserting that no individual could benefit (p. 789).
**B. Meta-analyses found a clearer benefit for hip osteoarthritis.** Wrong, Hip osteoarthritis is specifically emphasized in the finding of no clear benefit, not stronger benefit (p. 789).
**C. Meta-analyses found consistent benefit after correction for study bias.** Wrong, The absence of clear benefit persisted when study bias was addressed (p. 789).
**D. Meta-analyses found superiority supporting use as first-line treatment.** Wrong, The cited guidelines do not recommend viscosupplementation on the available evidence; the possible individual trial described follows failure of other options (p. 789).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 789.
ref: Hazzard Ch 52 — OSTEOARTHRITIS · Harrison Ch 382 — Approach to Articular and Musculoskeletal Disease

q: An 87-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and hypertension is seen in the emergency department after a fall at his assisted-living facility. His daughter reports two other falls during the past month. He takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Blood pressure is 138/82 sitting and 118/70 after three minutes standing. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which approach to his insomnia treatment is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Review trazodone and introduce a behavioral insomnia treatment plan
Increase trazodone because it improves orthostatic blood-pressure control
Replace trazodone with diphenhydramine as primary treatment for chronic insomnia
Retain trazodone because sustained benefit is established in nondepressed patients
explanation:
**Trazodone** is associated with daytime sleepiness and orthostatic hypotension, and its evidence for insomnia without depression is limited. Behavioral insomnia treatment is first-line therapy; these statements support reviewing trazodone rather than predicting a uniquely largest reduction in falls (p. 661).
"Trazadone has been associated with daytime sleepiness, headache, and orthostatic hypotension as well as priapism." (p. 661).
"It is the recommended first-line treatment for insomnia in all adults." (p. 661).

**A. Review trazodone and introduce a behavioral insomnia treatment plan.** Correct, it addresses the drug's relevant adverse effects while using the source-recommended behavioral treatment approach (p. 661; application).
**B. Increase trazodone because it improves orthostatic blood-pressure control.** Wrong, orthostatic hypotension is a reported adverse effect, not a condition that trazodone is described as improving (p. 661).
**C. Replace trazodone with diphenhydramine as primary treatment for chronic insomnia.** Wrong, diphenhydramine is specifically discouraged as primary insomnia treatment in older patients (p. 661).
**D. Retain trazodone because sustained benefit is established in nondepressed patients.** Wrong, in the cited study of nondepressed patients, short-term trazodone benefit dissipated after two weeks (p. 661).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 661.

q: An 83-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, orthostatic hypotension, and a neurogenic bladder is admitted with his third aspiration pneumonia. A suprapubic catheter was placed a year ago for urinary retention. His wife provides continuous care and appears exhausted. He is bedbound, nonverbal, and needs a pureed diet for dysphagia; his weight fell from 72 to 61 kg in six months. During palliative care planning, continued catheter use is chosen. Which maintenance approach follows Hazzard?
o: Plan routine catheter irrigation in the absence of obstruction
Plan catheter replacement at arbitrary fixed time intervals
Maintain closed drainage and keep urine flow unobstructed
Use daily povidone–iodine meatal care to reduce infection
explanation:
**Chronic catheter care** aims to minimize complications when catheterization remains indicated (pp. 715–716). The source directs staff to "Maintain closed sterile drainage" and "Maintain unobstructed urine flow" (p. 716).

**A. Plan routine catheter irrigation in the absence of obstruction.** Wrong, the source advises avoiding irrigation unless needed to prevent or relieve obstruction (p. 716).
**B. Plan catheter replacement at arbitrary fixed time intervals.** Wrong, the source advises against changing catheters at arbitrary fixed intervals (p. 716).
**C. Maintain closed drainage and keep urine flow unobstructed.** Correct, closed drainage and unobstructed flow are specifically recommended maintenance principles (p. 716).
**D. Use daily povidone–iodine meatal care to reduce infection.** Wrong, daily povidone–iodine meatal care is discouraged because it may increase infection rates (p. 716).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 716.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An older man taking an alpha blocker for hypertension reports dizziness on standing. Which property of this drug class is relevant to assessment?
o: A tendency to produce postural hypotension.
A tendency to protect against postural hypotension.
Fewer heart-failure admissions than thiazide-type diuretic monotherapy.
Preferred monotherapy for uncomplicated hypertension in older adults.
explanation:
**Alpha-1 receptor antagonists** have a "predilection to produce postural hypotension" (p. 1226). This is relevant to symptoms on standing. The source also reports greater heart-failure hospitalization risk than diuretic monotherapy and consequently limits their role as initial monotherapy (p. 1226).

**A. A tendency to produce postural hypotension.** Correct, the stated tendency to cause postural hypotension fits the symptom being assessed, without proving drug causation (p. 1226).
**B. A tendency to protect against postural hypotension.** Wrong, the source describes production of postural hypotension, not protection against it (p. 1226).
**C. Fewer heart-failure admissions than thiazide-type diuretic monotherapy.** Wrong, the trial comparison showed higher rather than lower heart-failure hospitalization risk with alpha-blocker monotherapy (p. 1226).
**D. Preferred monotherapy for uncomplicated hypertension in older adults.** Wrong, the source limits monotherapy to selected men with beneficial effects on prostatic symptoms rather than preferring it broadly for uncomplicated hypertension (p. 1226).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1226.
ref: Hazzard Ch 43 — FALLS · Harrison Ch 26 — Neurologic Causes of Weakness and Paralysis

q: A 75-year-old woman is being reviewed for osteoporosis one year after a hip fracture. She completed five years of alendronate before the fracture. Her hip T-score is now −1.3, previously −2.9; calcium is 9.6 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m², and 25-hydroxyvitamin D 35 ng/mL. She has difficulty remembering daily medication but reliably attends a weekly bridge club. During discussion of treatment options, which drug binds RANKL to inhibit osteoclast activation?
o: Zoledronic acid given by intravenous infusion
Teriparatide given by daily subcutaneous injection
Denosumab given by subcutaneous injection
Alendronate given as oral bisphosphonate treatment
explanation:
**Denosumab** targets RANKL, a mechanism distinct from bisphosphonate treatment or intermittent PTH analog therapy. Hazzard states that denosumab "binds to RANKL and inhibits osteoclast activation and activity" (p. 776). This identifies the drug mechanism; it does not establish a unique best treatment from this patient's renal function or previous fracture.

**A. Zoledronic acid given by intravenous infusion.** Wrong, zoledronic acid is a bisphosphonate; Hazzard distinguishes bisphosphonates from the RANKL-binding monoclonal antibody asked for here (pp. 773–774, 776).
**B. Teriparatide given by daily subcutaneous injection.** Wrong, intermittent teriparatide is a PTH analog with an anabolic effect on bone, rather than RANKL blockade (p. 776).
**C. Denosumab given by subcutaneous injection.** Correct, denosumab is the RANKL-binding monoclonal antibody described in the source (p. 776).
**D. Alendronate given as oral bisphosphonate treatment.** Wrong, alendronate is a bisphosphonate, not the RANKL-binding antibody specified in the question (pp. 773–774, 776).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 773–774, 776.

q: An 83-year-old woman has a COPD exacerbation with acute hypercarbia and respiratory acidosis. She is a candidate for noninvasive positive pressure ventilation and has no contraindication. What is the role of this treatment?
o: To reduce gas exchange and thereby reduce respiratory drive
To improve gas exchange and support the respiratory muscles
To replace bronchodilator treatment during the acute exacerbation
To increase breathing workload and train the respiratory muscles
explanation:
**Noninvasive positive pressure ventilation** supports breathing while medical treatment has time to improve airflow and reduce the work of breathing. In this setting it "improves gas exchange, improves breathing pattern, and provides support to the respiratory muscles" (p. 1257).

**A. To reduce gas exchange and thereby reduce respiratory drive.** Wrong, its stated role is to improve gas exchange, not reduce it (p. 1257).
**B. To improve gas exchange and support the respiratory muscles.** Correct, these are the supportive effects described for an exacerbation with acute hypercarbia and acidosis (p. 1257).
**C. To replace bronchodilator treatment during the acute exacerbation.** Wrong, the source describes ventilation as allowing time for bronchodilators and other medical therapy to work, not replacing them (p. 1257).
**D. To increase breathing workload and train the respiratory muscles.** Wrong, the described goal is support of the respiratory muscles while work of breathing is reduced, not an increase in their workload (p. 1257).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1257.
ref: Hazzard Ch 58 — DELIRIUM · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: An 82-year-old woman with dementia has persistent liquid fecal soiling after a period of constipation. Rectal examination finds impacted hard stool. Which interpretation best fits the source?
o: The soiling argues for liquid stool production without a retained-stool mechanism
The soiling argues for a bowel disorder in which rectal emptying is unhelpful
The soiling is consistent with overflow associated with retained rectal stool
The soiling is consistent with a condition that needs containment before assessment
explanation:
**Overflow fecal incontinence** can present as continuous soiling despite retained hard stool. Hazzard describes overflow as "continuous fecal soiling and fecal impaction on rectal examination" (p. 1361). The source emphasizes assessment and complete rectal emptying, followed by a maintenance regimen to prevent recurrence (p. 1361).

**A. The soiling argues for liquid stool production without a retained-stool mechanism.** Wrong, The combination of soiling and impaction matches the source's description of overflow; liquid leakage does not exclude a retained-stool mechanism (p. 1361).
**B. The soiling argues for a bowel disorder in which rectal emptying is unhelpful.** Wrong, The source reports effective resolution of overflow when complete rectal emptying was achieved, so retained stool is a treatment target (p. 1361).
**C. The soiling is consistent with overflow associated with retained rectal stool.** Correct, Both defining observations in the source description are present: continuing soiling and impaction on rectal examination (p. 1361).
**D. The soiling is consistent with a condition that needs containment before assessment.** Wrong, The source criticizes inadequate assessment and unnecessarily conservative containment with pads; recognizing and treating the impaction is required (p. 1361).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1361.
ref: Hazzard Ch 87 — CONSTIPATION · Harrison Ch 49 — Diarrhea and Constipation

q: An 88-year-old patient with terminal metastatic cancer and an expected survival of weeks develops a sacral pressure injury with eschar, described as a Kennedy terminal ulcer. Which goal is consistent with palliative pressure-injury care in Hazzard?
o: Make complete wound closure the principal target of the care plan.
Make comfort and reduction of wound-related distress the principal target.
Make frequent dressing changes the principal target despite their burden.
Make a fixed repositioning schedule the principal target despite discomfort.
explanation:
**Palliative pressure-injury care** focuses on comfort and limiting the wound's impact when healing is not the intent (p. 698). Hazzard states: “Palliative PI care means that the goals are comfort and limiting the extent or impact of the PI but without the intent of healing” (p. 698). Pain control, management of odorous drainage, absorptive dressings, and adjustment of repositioning to ease burden serve that goal.

**A. Make complete wound closure the principal target of the care plan.** Wrong, The source defines palliative care without the intent of healing; complete closure is not its principal goal (p. 698).
**B. Make comfort and reduction of wound-related distress the principal target.** Correct, Comfort and limiting the wound's impact are the explicit goals described for palliative care, which may be appropriate in terminal cancer (p. 698).
**C. Make frequent dressing changes the principal target despite their burden.** Wrong, Highly absorptive dressings are recommended to reduce dressing-change frequency, rather than making frequent changes the goal despite burden (p. 698).
**D. Make a fixed repositioning schedule the principal target despite discomfort.** Wrong, The source allows repositioning time frames to be adjusted or lengthened to ease patient burden, rather than prioritizing a rigid schedule despite discomfort (p. 698).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 698.

q: Why is a bedside BIA result less definitive than a direct measurement of muscle function?
o: It directly measures the SPPB balance and chair-stand components
It estimates mass using population- and device-specific equations and cutoffs
It directly measures gait speed
It directly measures grip strength
explanation:
BIA is useful at the bedside, but its population- and device-specific equations and cutoffs lack standardization and limit accuracy (p735); mass estimates have weaker links to outcomes (p732).

D. It directly measures grip strength: Grip is a strength measurement; BIA estimates muscle mass (p735).
C. It directly measures gait speed: Gait speed is a physical-performance measure; BIA estimates mass (p735).
A. It directly measures the SPPB balance and chair-stand components: Those components belong to physical-performance assessment; BIA instead estimates mass (p735).

q: Why does internal fixation suit intertrochanteric fractures?
o: Its blood supply depends on the delicate vessels closely apposed to the femoral neck
Internal fixation requires replacing the joint with an arthroplasty
Nonunion and osteonecrosis are more common in this region
The blood supply to the intertrochanteric area is plentiful and redundant
explanation:
The intertrochanteric blood supply is plentiful and redundant, allowing fractures to heal well after internal fixation (p794).

A. Its blood supply depends on the delicate vessels closely apposed to the femoral neck: That is the femoral-neck/head vascular pattern, contrasted with the intertrochanteric area (p794).
C. Nonunion and osteonecrosis are more common in this region: They are less common in the intertrochanteric region (p794).
B. Internal fixation requires replacing the joint with an arthroplasty: The book distinguishes fixation with a plate/screw or intramedullary screw from joint replacement (p794).
